comparison: Both strongly support the core behavioral finding that Cdk5 knockdown selectively abolishes phase delays while preserving phase advances. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence across multiple time points and protocols (C5-C7, C49-C60), while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as the study's central contribution with quotes from all reviewers confirming the convincing demonstration of Cdk5's gating role.

Both support the molecular findings on Cdk5-p35 complex dynamics (C64-C68). OpenEval notes the paradoxical p35 increase with decreased Cdk5 activity is explained by reduced complex formation, though the mechanism remains unclear. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the high-standard molecular work without challenge, acknowledging the study provides missing mechanistic details.

Both support the immunohistochemistry data showing constitutive phosphorylation of CREB-S133, CaMKII, and CaMKIV in shCdk5 animals (C73-C79). OpenEval also includes protein localization findings (C80-C83). Peer reviewers explicitly accept the PKA-CaMK-CREB signaling pathway mechanism as providing missing molecular details, with no challenges to the immunohistochemistry data.

Perfect agreement on calcium imaging data (C88-C89). OpenEval supports the fiber photometry findings showing reduced calcium responses in shCdk5 mice, noting the mechanism requires further investigation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the neural activity imaging as convincing evidence bridging behavioral to molecular experiments.

Both support the FRET data on CREB phosphorylation dynamics (C92-C94, C96). OpenEval notes the indirect measurement and DMSO artifact exclusion as potential limitations. Peer reviewers praise the non-trivial, high-standard experiments and accept the overall mechanistic model without challenging the FRET approach.

Both support the immunoprecipitation data showing differential CREB interaction with p-CaMKIV versus p-PKA (C97-C99). OpenEval cautions about interpreting negative results (no PKA-CREB interaction) due to potential technical limitations. Peer reviewers accept this mechanistic detail as well-presented and appropriately described without raising concerns.

Both support the DARPP32-PKA regulatory mechanism (C101-C106). OpenEval notes statistical support but incomplete explanation of how light reduces DARPP32 phosphorylation. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the missing mechanistic details for the PKA-CaMK-CREB pathway, with experiments done to high standard.

Both support PKA-Cav3.1 interaction data (C108-C110). OpenEval notes co-localization doesn't prove direct interaction and suggests functional validation would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall gating mechanism without specific concerns about the co-localization approach.

Both support the qPCR data on light-inducible genes (C113-C119). OpenEval emphasizes selective effects and differential regulation of Per1/Dec1 versus Per2/Dec2/Bmal1. Peer reviewers accept the gene expression data as well-presented with strongly supported conclusions, part of the comprehensive experimental framework.

Both support the cell culture validation experiments (C134-C136). OpenEval emphasizes the in vitro system validates in vivo findings and demonstrates cell-autonomous effects. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the high-standard combination of molecular, cellular, and behavioral techniques.

Both support the integrative model that Cdk5 gates both arms of the light response (C138, C140, C146, C148, C158). OpenEval notes some mechanistic details remain unclear. Peer reviewers strongly endorse the overall model, with Reviewer 1 stating results strongly support conclusions and Reviewer 2 happy with the manuscript, indicating full acceptance of the integrated framework.

OpenEval notes this is a negative result with alternative interpretations. Peer reviewers accept this finding as helping define the boundaries of Cdk5's mechanism without challenge.

Both support altered localization of CAM and Cav3.1 (C80-C83). OpenEval emphasizes Cdk5's role in protein trafficking consistent with literature. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall PKA-CaMK-CREB mechanism without specific discussion of the localization findings.
